options.title: What if a bridge joined Russia and America?
options.first_line: What if a bridge joined Russia and America?
options.first_frame: The globe from space with Russia and the United States lit in their flags, a glowing bridge line drawing itself across the narrow sea at the top of the world where they almost touch.

options.title: What if you could drive from Russia to Alaska?
options.first_line: What if you could drive from Russia to Alaska, over the sea?
options.first_frame: A car on the tip of Russia facing a narrow strip of sea, Alaska on the other side, a road sign pointing across the water to ALASKA.

options.title: What if one bridge crossed the Bering Strait?
options.first_line: Russia and America nearly touch at one strait. What if a single bridge joined them?
options.first_frame: A close map of the Bering Strait with Russia's coast on the left and Alaska on the right, two small islands in the middle, a bridge half built between them.

why: Driving a car from Russia to Alaska over the sea is something a stranger can picture doing themselves, the ALASKA road sign pointing across the water tells the story with the sound off, and it raises a how-is-that-possible question without giving away the answer.
